topic: How Multilayer Perceptrons (MLP) Store Knowledge in Transformers
target_audience: Undergraduate students in Computer Science or AI enthusiasts

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Two-Part Architecture
lecture_lines: Transformer blocks feature attention and MLPs.
Attention is the dynamic reader of context.
MLPs act as static fact storage.
Think of librarians reading specific books.
Information resides permanently in the MLP.
animations: Highlight 'Attention' box in #FFD700 when line 2 is read.
Highlight 'MLP' box in #FF4500 when line 3 is read.
Animate a flow arrow between them changing color to #00FFFF.
Flash both boxes simultaneously to indicate interaction.

sections.title: The MLP as a Key-Value Memory
lecture_lines: First layers detect specific input patterns.
Second layers project associated factual values.
animations: Display an MLP weight matrix. Label #FFFFFF.
Animate specific neuron paths activation in #FF4500.
Fade in 'Memory' text near the active path in #FFFFFF.

sections.title: How Facts are Coded in Weights
lecture_lines: Facts are encoded in weight vectors.
Inputs push weights toward specific outputs.
animations: Show a weight vector changing color from blue to red.
Visualize input moving through the weight grid.
Flash the resulting activated neurons in #00FF00.

sections.title: The 'Locality' of Knowledge
lecture_lines: Knowledge is localized to neuron clusters.
Different domains occupy different weight paths.
Fine-tuning may disrupt existing localized facts.
animations: Show the large matrix with highlighted clusters.
Highlight one concept cluster in #FF00FF with a boundary box.
Show surrounding weights remaining in static grey color.

sections.title: Summary and Synthesis
lecture_lines: MLPs are compressed, distributed knowledge databases.
Knowledge emerges from collaborative weighted connections.
It is a complex, structural collaboration.
animations: Place icons for Mapper, Memory, Weights, and Locality on screen.
